newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivorian cocoa exports seen at 534,000 T end Feb.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian cocoa exports seen at 534,000 T end Feb.

text.p: Cocoa exports from Ivory Coast totalled 534,000 tonnes in the first five months of the 1996/97 season against 553,238 tonnes officially recorded for the same period in the 1995/96 record crop year, port sources said.
The sources put exports at 121,000 tonnes in February, 150,000 tonnes in January, 122,000 tonnes in December, 131,000 tonnes in November and 10,000 tonnes in October -- giving 534,000 tonnes.
Official shipping data showed Ivory Coast cocoa bean exports of 166,268 tonnes of cocoa beans in December, 130,525 tonnes in November and 5,434 tonnes in October.
Complete data were not immediately available for January and February but 99,525 tonnes left Abidjan in January.
Monthly figures take around a month to be compiled.

Ivory Coast, the world's largest cocoa producer, had a record 1.2 million tonne crop in 1995/96. It originally forecast 950,000 tonnes for 1996/97 but Commodities Minister Guy-Alain Gauze said this week that it had produced 800,000 tonnes and had no more to sell.
Some private forecasters have upgraded their estimates to closer to 1.1 million tonnes.
